_doc: Macros that two or more headers define with different values, as they stood after the one-time triage of 2026-08-18 (KNOWN_ISSUES ARCH-2). scripts/check_consistency.py fails on any name NOT listed here, and also when a listed name stops conflicting — so the list cannot rot quietly. Measured at triage time: no translation unit sees two variants of the same macro, so every entry is latent, not live. Categories are guidance for whoever picks this up, not enforced.

_categories.magic-type-split: Format signature defined as an INTEGER in uft_format_parsers.h and as a STRING elsewhere. The dangerous class: passing the integer to memcmp() dereferences it. This already crashed MF-418 with UFT_SCP_SIGNATURE. Fix by choosing one representation per format and deleting the other.
_categories.platform-boilerplate: Compiler/platform plumbing defined in parallel in uft_compiler.h, uft_config.h, uft_platform.h, uft_common.h, uft_packed.h and compat/uft_platform.h. Values agree per platform, so the defect is five parallel headers rather than the values. UFT_PACKED is the exception: attribute vs pragma is a real usage-model difference (ARCH-1).
_categories.name-too-generic: Two DIFFERENT formats using the same unqualified name -- Atari DOS vs C64 BAM for DIR_ENTRY_SIZE, C64 TAP vs Sinclair TAP for TAP_BLOCK_*. Neither value is wrong; the names are. Fix by prefixing.
_categories.format-constant: Same format, contradictory values across headers. At most one can be right. 86F and IMD are both tier T3, so the winner cannot be picked without an authoritative source -- do not guess.
